question: In the core of logical-mathematical relationships and quantification, a preschool educator conducts the following learning experience with the children: in small groups, she asks them to take two bars of plasticine with the same amount, to make a big ball with one and small balls with the other. Then, she asks the children: "Where do you think there is more plasticine?". Considering the presented situation, which logical-mathematical reasoning skill is promoted with this activity?

A 6th-grade teacher is tackling the unit on triangles and designs an activity where students are asked to construct four triangles with side lengths of: Triangle 1: 12 cm, 5 cm and 11 cm. Triangle 2: 12 cm, 5 cm and 9 cm. Triangle 3: 12 cm, 5 cm and 7 cm. Triangle 4: 12 cm, 5 cm and 5 cm. Then, they are asked to observe their constructions and compare them with their peers to verify that everyone observes the same thing. What is the main learning objective of the activity described above?
answer_a: Compare triangles according to the length of their sides and angles
answer_b: Make conjectures about necessary conditions for the construction of triangles
answer_c: Draw conclusions regarding the relationship between the sides and angles of a triangle
answer_d: Classify triangles according to the length of their sides by explaining classification criteria

question: A second-year high school teacher has completed the unit on real numbers with his students and wants to evaluate if they are capable of solving problems that do not have solutions within the set of rational numbers. Which of the following assessment activities will allow the teacher to obtain information about this?
answer_a: Determine the height of an equilateral triangle with side 2
answer_b: Approximate irrational numbers from below and above
answer_c: Locate square roots on the number line, explaining the procedure used
answer_d: Determine the lengths of the legs of an isosceles right triangle whose hypotenuse measures 2/sqrt(2)
